oneLiner: A leveraged call option on AI capex: $104B take-or-pay backlog and 112% growth against $20B+ of ~11% debt, deeply negative FCF, and GPUs that depreciate faster than the loans amortize.
thesis: Backlog is the story: $104.2B (+246% YoY) of committed, largely take-or-pay contracts - OpenAI ~$22.4B, Meta ~$35B implied, new Anthropic agreement, $6B Jane Street; NVIDIA provides a $6.3B capacity backstop through 2032.
Speed and NVIDIA allocation priority are the edge: first to deploy new generations at scale (Vera Rubin ships Q3 2026; 120K Blackwell Ultra GPUs planned in a UK data center by end-2026).
The model only works if contract pricing holds through renewal cycles and capital markets stay open: Q2 interest expense ($640M) was 5x adjusted operating income ($128M).
Diversification is improving (Microsoft was ~67% of FY2025 revenue; Meta, Anthropic, Jane Street added since) but the top two were still 65% of Q1 2026 revenue.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 2026 (reported Aug 11, 2026 - after close today)
points: Revenue $2.58B, +112% YoY, +24% QoQ (beat); stock jumped ~13% after hours.
Adjusted operating income $128M (5% margin); GAAP net loss $626M; interest expense $640M.
FCF roughly negative $5.7B in the quarter; FY2026 capex guide $31-35B.
Guide: Q3 revenue $3.4-3.6B (~+158% YoY mid); FY2026 raised to $12.4-13.2B revenue, $960M-1.15B adjusted operating income.

segments: GPU cloud (neocloud) renting NVIDIA-based AI capacity under multi-year committed contracts.

Debt-funded buildout: total debt in the $21-35B range depending on definition/date (sources conflict); $2.6B delayed-draw term loan closed Aug 10, 2026. Core Scientific acquisition failed (CORZ holders voted it down Oct 2025); commercial collaboration continues.
competitive: Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI) plus neoclouds: Nebius, Crusoe, Lambda, RunPod.
On-demand H100 pricing has fragmented (~$1.49-6.98/hr across providers); CEO says Blackwell/Vera Rubin contract pricing is setting new highs while prior-gen holds.
Neocloud industry revenue exceeded $25B in 2025; customers (Microsoft, Meta) are also building their own capacity.
moat: Scale, NVIDIA allocation priority, and $104B of contracted take-or-pay revenue - not technology. GPUs are a commodity every competitor can buy; the edge is deployment speed, financing access, and switching friction inside multi-year contracts.
risks: Leverage: ~$20B+ debt at high-single-digit to ~11% rates; interest already exceeds adjusted operating income.
Customer concentration: top two customers 65% of Q1 2026 revenue; OpenAI's funding capacity is a counterparty risk.
GPU depreciation/obsolescence: 6-year depreciation vs ~3-year product cycles; residual-value risk on prior-gen fleets.
Renewal/repricing risk when initial terms expire into a lower spot market.
Negative FCF (-$5.7B in Q2 alone) requires continuous capital-market access; credit tightening is existential.
Kerrisdale-style critiques: circular financing dynamics with NVIDIA flatter demand.
catalysts: Vera Rubin shipments beginning Q3 2026; UK 120K-GPU deployment by end-2026.
Hyperscaler 2027 capex guidance as demand proxy.
pricedIn: At ~$50B market cap plus $30B+ net debt, EV is roughly $80B+ vs ~$12.8B FY2026 guided revenue: ~6x EV/revenue on hypergrowth, ~24x EV/EBITDA. Bulls see the backlog making the equity a leveraged call on AI capex with visibility through 2030+. Bears argue returns on capital never clear an ~11% cost of debt.

scenarios.bear: AI capex decelerates in 2027, spot GPU prices slide, a major customer fails to fund commitments; backlog converts slowly, prior-gen fleets get written down, refinancing $20B+ against negative FCF forces dilution or asset sales; equity de-rates toward 2-3x sales ($40-60).
scenarios.base: FY2026 lands near guidance (~$12.8B revenue, ~$1B adjusted operating income); backlog converts on schedule; interest stabilizes with scale; diversification reduces single-customer risk; stock trades with AI sentiment around 5-7x forward sales (~$100-140).
scenarios.bull: Q3 guide proves conservative; 2027 revenue exceeds $20B as backlog ramps; Vera Rubin pricing holds premium; adjusted operating margin reaches mid-teens; leverage turns accretive and the stock revisits $153+.

valPresets.note: FCF-based DCF is meaningless while FCF runs at -$5.7B/quarter. This mode grows revenue, applies a horizon FCF margin and an exit multiple, and nets off today's debt. Interim burn is ignored -- generous to the bull case.
